canonical_name: Hasse-Minkowski theorem for quadratic forms over number fields
canonical_statement: Let K be a number field, V a finite-dimensional K-vector space, and q a nondegenerate quadratic form on V. Then q has a nonzero isotropic vector over K if and only if its scalar extension has a nonzero isotropic vector over the completion K_v for every place v of K.
domain_and_universes: K a number field; V a finite-dimensional K-vector space; q a nondegenerate quadratic form on V; exact Lean universes remain to be fixed
quantifiers: for every finite-dimensional K-vector space V
for every nondegenerate quadratic form q on V
for every place v of K in the local condition
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of the rational numbers
conclusion: Global isotropy of q is equivalent to isotropy after scalar extension to K_v for every place v of K.

alternate_encodings.target: A homogeneous quadratic polynomial has a nontrivial zero over K iff it has one over every K_v
